# Appendix E: Build Flags

Flags set with `-define:NAME=value` on `vidar run`, `check`, `test` and `build`. Vidar reads some of them itself and passes all of them on to `odin`, where the generated code reads them with `#config`.

| Flag | Default |
|---|---|
| [`VIDAR_CLOSURE_ENV`](#vidar_closure_env) | `128` |
| [`VIDAR_FILES_ON_WORKERS`](#vidar_files_on_workers) | `ODIN_OS != .Linux` |
| [`VIDAR_RACE`](#vidar_race) | `false` |
| [`VIDAR_RACE_TABLE`](#vidar_race_table) | `1 &lt;&lt; 16` |
| [`VIDAR_SCHED_DEBUG`](#vidar_sched_debug) | `ODIN_OPTIMIZATION_MODE &lt; .Speed` |
| [`VIDAR_SCHED_TRACE`](#vidar_sched_trace) | `false` |
| [`VIDAR_STACK_SIZE`](#vidar_stack_size) | `256 * mem.Kilobyte` |
| [`VIDAR_THREADS`](#vidar_threads) | `1` |
| [`VIDAR_TRACE_EVENTS`](#vidar_trace_events) | `1 &lt;&lt; 16` |
| [`VIDAR_WORKERS`](#vidar_workers) | `4` |

## `VIDAR_CLOSURE_ENV`

Default: `128`.

A closure: a proc plus a copy of its captures, inline; -define:VIDAR_CLOSURE_ENV=&lt;bytes&gt; sets the room.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_CLOSURE_ENV=256    # closures that capture up to 256 bytes
```

Every closure value grows with it, so arrays and channels of closures do too. See [How Big a Closure Is](ch04-03-closure-types.md#how-big-a-closure-is).

## `VIDAR_FILES_ON_WORKERS`

Default: `ODIN_OS != .Linux`.

Send file operations to worker threads. On by default except on Linux, where io_uring does them; set it to true on Linux to test that path.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_FILES_ON_WORKERS=true   # on Linux: files through workers, not io_uring
```

## `VIDAR_RACE`

Default: `false`.

-define:VIDAR_RACE=true, given to vidar too (it marks the writes to watch): reports two writes to a global or a captured local, from different goroutines, with nothing ordering them.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_RACE=true -define:VIDAR_THREADS=4
```

Give it to `vidar` itself (`run`, `build`, `check`), not only to `odin`: Vidar marks the writes to watch when it sees the define. See [Race Check](ch14-06-debugging.md#race-check).

## `VIDAR_RACE_TABLE`

Default: `1 << 16`.

How many addresses the race check watches (a power of two). It stops adding at 3/4 full.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_RACE=true -define:VIDAR_RACE_TABLE=262144
```

## `VIDAR_SCHED_DEBUG`

Default: `ODIN_OPTIMIZATION_MODE < .Speed`.

Where each goroutine started and what it waits on, printed on a deadlock and on SIGQUIT; on unless built with -o:speed (-define:VIDAR_SCHED_DEBUG=true turns it on there, false turns it off).

```bash
vidar build . -bin -define:VIDAR_SCHED_DEBUG=true -- -o:speed   # keep the goroutine dump in a fast build
```

## `VIDAR_SCHED_TRACE`

Default: `false`.

Each thread keeps its last TRACE_EVENTS scheduler events (go, run, park, wake, steal, I/O, idle), written at exit, on a deadlock and on SIGQUIT as Chrome trace JSON (Perfetto, chrome://tracing) to vidar-trace.json, or to the file $VIDAR_TRACE_FILE names.

```bash
VIDAR_TRACE_FILE=/tmp/trace.json vidar run . -define:VIDAR_SCHED_TRACE=true
```

Open the file in [Perfetto](https://ui.perfetto.dev). See [The Scheduler Trace](ch14-06-debugging.md#the-scheduler-trace).

## `VIDAR_STACK_SIZE`

Default: `256 * mem.Kilobyte`.

The stack of each goroutine, in bytes, with a guard page below it.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_STACK_SIZE=1048576    # 1 MB per goroutine
```

## `VIDAR_THREADS`

Default: `1`.

Goroutines run on this many threads; above 1, each thread runs its own scheduler, and an idle thread takes half of another's runnable goroutines.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_THREADS=4
```

See [Running on Several Threads](ch14-05-threads.md).

## `VIDAR_TRACE_EVENTS`

Default: `1 << 16`.

How many scheduler events each thread keeps for the trace (a power of two).

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_SCHED_TRACE=true -define:VIDAR_TRACE_EVENTS=1048576
```

## `VIDAR_WORKERS`

Default: `4`.

How many worker threads run `sched.blocking` calls, file operations off Linux, and DNS lookups.

```bash
vidar run . -define:VIDAR_WORKERS=16     # more threads for sched.blocking and DNS
```
